accepted.trend: UPI MDR For Capital Markets: Why A Tiny Fee Could Test India’s Zero-brokerage Model
accepted.context: Urban Indians in their late 20s and early 30s are heavily investing in mutual funds and stocks via apps, only to find micro-fees eating into their small gains.
accepted.angle: Every transaction now has a micro-fee chipping away at your ₹5,000 mutual fund SIP.
slides: Log in to your investment app today.

Transfer ₹5,000 — UPI fee.
Buy mutual fund — stamp duty.
Sell share — DP charges.
Withdraw money — GST.

The market went down 2% today.

The brokers made their cut.
accepted.caption: Your financial independence has a subscription model. 📈

accepted.trend: UPI MDR For Capital Markets: Why A Tiny Fee Could Test India’s Zero-brokerage Model
accepted.context: Urban Indians who jumped on the 'zero-brokerage' retail investing bandwagon are realizing free services do not exist.
accepted.angle: The illusion of the 'zero-brokerage' era is masking an endless stream of micro-taxes.
slides: Open your portfolio app and look at the 'zero' fees.

Zero brokerage on equity.
₹15 per order on options.
18% GST on the platform fee.
₹2 transaction tax per transfer.

It is free to lose your money.

It costs money to move it.
accepted.caption: Free admission. Paid exit. 💸
